title: Luke Bible Quiz - Chapter 19
description: Ten questions on Luke 19: Zacchaeus in the sycamore tree, the parable of the ten minas, and the entry towards Jerusalem.

questions.text: Why did Zacchaeus climb up into a sycamore tree?
questions.explanation: He was trying to see who Jesus was and could not because of the crowd, since he was short, so he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree.

answers.text: Because the crowd had driven him away
Because he was hiding from the tax collectors
Because Jesus had told him to wait there
Because he was short and could not see over the crowd

questions.text: What did Zacchaeus promise to do for the poor and for anyone he had wronged?
questions.explanation: Zacchaeus said he would give half of his goods to the poor, and restore four times as much to anyone from whom he had wrongfully exacted anything.

answers.text: Give all his goods away and follow him
Give half his goods away and restore four times as much
Pay back a tenth of all that he had taken
Give two denarii to each poor man in Jericho

questions.text: How many servants did the nobleman call, and what did he give them?
questions.explanation: He called ten servants of his and gave them ten mina coins, telling them to conduct business until he came.

answers.text: Twelve servants, with twelve baskets
Three servants, with a hundred denarii
Ten servants, with ten mina coins
Two servants, with two denarii

questions.text: What did the nobleman give the servant whose mina had made ten more?
questions.explanation: He called him a good servant and said that, because he was found faithful with very little, he would have authority over ten cities.

answers.text: Authority over ten cities
Authority over five cities
A seat at his table
Ten more mina coins to invest

questions.text: Another servant brought his mina back - where had he kept it?
questions.explanation: That servant said he had kept the mina laid away in a handkerchief, because he feared his lord.

answers.text: Buried in the ground
Deposited in the bank
Hidden in his lord's house
Laid away in a handkerchief

questions.text: What did he say the disciples would find in the village?
questions.explanation: He said they would find a colt tied, which no man had ever sat upon, and they were to untie it and bring it.

answers.text: A colt tied, which no man had ever sat upon
An ox and a donkey in a stall
A house prepared for him
Two men who would guide them

questions.text: What did the people do with their cloaks as he went?
questions.explanation: They threw their cloaks on the colt, and as he went they spread their cloaks on the road.

answers.text: They waved them in the air
They spread them on the road
They tore them in grief
They laid them at the temple gate

questions.text: What did he answer the Pharisees who told him to rebuke his disciples?
questions.explanation: He answered that if these were silent, the stones would cry out.

answers.text: That the disciples knew what they were saying
That the Pharisees should praise God too
That the stones would cry out if they were silent
That he would rebuke them in Jerusalem

questions.text: What did he do when he came near and saw the city?
questions.explanation: When he came near, he saw the city and wept over it, saying that the things which belong to its peace were now hidden from its eyes.

answers.text: He wept over it
He blessed it from the mountain
He turned back to Jericho
He sent two disciples into it

questions.text: What did he say the temple had been made into?
questions.explanation: He drove out those who bought and sold, saying that it is written, "My house is a house of prayer," but they had made it a "den of robbers".

answers.text: A marketplace of the nations
A house of mourning
A place of hidden graves
A den of robbers
